title: Strum C then A minor on a ukulele, all strings ringing
instruction: Play C on the ukulele: four even downstrums, then pluck its fretted string once to check it; then four of A minor and check its G and A strings the same way, and keep holding the A minor.
context: Why: C (third fret of the A string) and A minor (second fret of the G string) are the first two chords taught, and teachers have players fret a chord and pluck its strings one at a time to check none is muted. The robot must work out how to press one outer string just behind its fret wire hard enough to ring without touching the open string beside it, keep that press still while the other hand strums evenly across all four, and move to the other outer string within 2.5 s. Done by: millions of beginners, school music classes and players accompanying songs.
setup: Table 75 cm high. Concert ukulele (Kala KA-C, satin mahogany, 608 mm long, 376.2 mm scale, 36.5 mm fingerboard at the nut, 18 nickel frets 1 mm proud, Aquila Super Nylgut concert set, high G, tuned G4-C4-E4-A4 at 4.37, 3.91, 4.41 and 4.72 kg tension) lying face up in a padded cradle screwed to the table: foam body rest under the body, foam neck rest under the neck, hook-and-loop strap over the lower bout. The neck points to the robot's left, the centre line 22 cm in front of the arm bases, the nut 23 cm left of centre; the G string is on the far side and the A string nearest the robot. The strings run 9.2 cm above the table, 1.5 mm above the fret wire crowns; the first three frets sit 21.1 mm, 41.0 mm and 59.9 mm from the nut, and the strings are 10.0 mm apart at the frets and 12.3 mm apart over the strum zone. Clip-on chromatic tuner on the headstock. A phone on a stand films the strum zone from 30 cm above at 240 fps (slow motion) beside a mm scale laid across the body; a second phone films the fretting hand beside a mm scale on the fingerboard's edge. Both grippers start at their ready poses, empty. No other objects.
scoring: Fret windows (from the nut): C = the A string, the fretting contact between the 41.0 mm and 59.9 mm fret wires; A minor = the G string, between 21.1 and 41.0 mm. Fretted = that string pressed 1.5 mm onto its fret wires with nothing touching it past the window's bridge-side wire, and the fretting hand touching no other string. Strum zone: the 80 mm of string past the fingerboard. Strike = a fingertip pushing a string 1.5 mm sideways in the strum zone (0.82-0.99 N at that string's stiffness), after which it slips off. Downstrum = a fingertip striking G, C, E and A in that order within 0.3 s. A struck string rings if nothing touches it for 0.5 s after. Check pluck = one outer string struck with no other within 0.3 s, ringing with the chord kept fretted for the 0.5 s after. Real trial, string by string (never by pitch: the fretted G and open A of A minor are both A4, and C4's harmonic is C5): a phone films the strum zone from above at 240 fps (shutter 1/250 s or slower, else dim the room or use a manual-shutter app; check first that a plucked string blurs) beside a mm scale; a ringing string shows a band at least 2 mm across in full (string included; under 1 mm at rest), read anywhere along its 80 mm, in every frame from 0.1 to 0.5 s after the strum, a muted or unstruck one a sharp line. In each strum all four strings must blur, each read on its own line: C = G, C, E and the fretted A; A minor = the fretted G, C, E and A. Each fretted string is also checked alone by its check pluck: blurred the same way, and on the clip-on tuner within 20 cents (C: A string C5; A minor: G string A4, then the open A string A4); the fretting tip moving no more than 2 mm from a block's first strum to its check plucks. 0 if the ukulele moves over 5 mm in its cradle (permanent). 0.25: four downstrums with C fretted and its open strings ringing (real trial: all four blurred). 0.5: as 0.25, then the C check pluck of the A string with the tip unmoved. 0.75: as 0.5, then four A minor downstrums with its open strings ringing (real trial: all four blurred), then the G check pluck and the open A check pluck, the tip unmoved. 1.0: as 0.75, with exactly four strums in each block at intervals within 25% of the block's mean, at most 2.5 s from the end of the C check's 0.5 s ring to the first A minor strum, and for the last 2 s the A minor still fretted, the fretting tip within 2 mm and the strumming gripper at least 20 mm from every string (both videos against their mm scales).
reset_notes: Retune to G4-C4-E4-A4 with the clip-on tuner before each trial; check the cradle strap; both arms to their ready poses.
fidelity: Ukulele and cradle rigid at real size. Strings are drawn lines except two parts: each chord's fret window, a 2 mm slider (0.5 N at rest, 2 N pressed 1.5 mm onto its frets), and each 80 mm strummed segment, sprung sideways at the string's stiffness (550-660 N/m): carried 1.5 mm it is struck, then drops under the tip (declared slip rule). Touching a drawn line mutes by rule. No sound. Static = dynamic friction.
